events.text: Newmont's Soaring Unit Costs Warrant Caution: Can It Protect Margins?
events.context:
Newmont's Soaring Unit Costs Warrant Caution: Can It Protect Margins?
Newmont Corporation’s NEM first-quarter 2025 results show concerning increases in unit costs. Its gold costs applicable to sales rose 16% year over year to $1,227 per ounce. All-in sustaining costs (AISC) — the most important cost metric of miners — were $1,651 per ounce for the same period, reflecting a roughly 13% sequential and 15% year-over-year increase. The rise was attributed to a decline in production due to non-core asset divestments as Newmont shifts its focus to Tier 1 assets.

events.text: Newmont (NEM) Secures Ghana Mining Lease Renewal With US$770 Million Deal
events.context:
Newmont (NEM) Secures Ghana Mining Lease Renewal With US$770 Million Deal
Newmont recently reported a series of significant events, including the renewal of the Akyem East Mining Lease in Ghana, receipt of substantial proceeds from its divestiture program, and a share buyback authorization up to $3 billion. As Newmont's capital allocation priorities focus on reducing debt and returning capital to shareholders, its price rose by 21% over the last quarter. This was during a period when broader markets like the S&P 500 posted gains amid strong corporate earnings, before experiencing declines due to trade tensions and a weaker-than-expected U.S. jobs report. These events provided support to Newmont’s gains, despite broader market volatility.
